texts.preamble: Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman Writ Petition No.27606 Of 2024 Oral Order
texts.facts: 3. This Writ Petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondents, more particularly respondent No.4 in binding over the petitioner under Sections - 126, 127, 128 and 129 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') on the request made by respondent No.5 and obtaining bond on 30.08.2024 vide Form No.13 for a period of six months without following due process of law as illegal and arbitrary, and for consequential direction to the respondents to permit him to do KL,J cultivation/agricultural operations on his land in Survey No.74/1/A, admeasuring Acs.14.09 guntas, situated at Gurvapur Village, Kasipet Mandal, Mancherial District. 4. The petitioner is claiming that he is the absolute owner and possessor of land admeasuring Ac.14.0900 gts., in Sy.No.74/1/A, situated at Gurvapur Village, Kasipet Mandal, Mancherial District, on the strength of a registered sale deed vide Document No.334 of 2020, dated 11.02.2020. According to him, respondent Nos.6 to 9 are continuously interfering with his possession under the guise of forged sale deeds and also threatened him to sell the subject land to them under the mediation of respondent No.4. He gave a report with respondent No.5 against the respondent Nos.6 to 9. However, the police, instead of registering FIR, advised him to settle the matter, otherwise, his life would be in danger, as respondent Nos.6 to 9 are having political influence. Further, the petitioner enquired about the ownership and title of adjacent land i.e., Sy.No.74/1 with respondent No.4 and obtained copies of sale deeds which the unofficial respondents have created by impersonating a dead person. The petitioner has KL,J filed sale deeds of respondent Nos.6 to 9 vide registered Document Nos.13287 of 2016, dated 26.10.2016, 13288 of 2016, 13293 of 2016, and 13294 of 2016, dated 25.10.2016 and further submitted that in all the above sale deeds, one Yousuf Ali Baig is the vendor who died on 15.04.2011, i.e., much prior to execution of sale deeds in favour of unofficial respondents. He further submitted that the Judgment dated 22.11.2022 passed by learned XX Junior Civil Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad in O.S.No.1549 of 2021 would also reflect that Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/ 1 Yousuf Ali Baig, who is the vendor of unofficial respondent Nos.6 to 9 died on 15.04.2011, which is clearly an impersonation of dead person at the time of registration of the sale deeds. He further stated that he has also submitted several representations to respondent Nos.1 to 5 along with documentary evidence. However, no action has been taken against respondent Nos.6 to 9 as they are influential persons. 5. While matter stood thus, pursuant to the report submitted by respondent No.5 on 30.08.2024, respondent No.4 bound over the petitioner under Sections - 126, 127, 128 and 129 of the BNSS by way of accepting bonds for keeping good behavior for a period KL,J of six (06) months forcibly, or else to forfeit an amount of Rs.50,000/- without following any procedure laid down under law. On account of the said action of respondent Nos.4 and 5, the petitioner herein is unable to attend agricultural operations on the subject land by way of cultivation, and thereby his livelihood is being affected. 6. Perusal of record would show that respondent Nos.6 to 9 said to have created sale deeds and got registered the adjacent property in their names as their Vendor died much prior to the execution of the said sale deeds i.e., 15.04.2011.
texts.arguments: In view of the above submission, it is apt to refer to Section - 129 of the BNSS, which is as under: "129. Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders. When an Executive Magistrate receives information that there is within his local jurisdiction a person who- (a) - - - - -, (b) - - - - -, or (c) - - - - -, or (d) - - - - -, or (e) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, offences, involving a breach of the peace, or (f) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of- Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/ 2 (i) any offence under one or more of the following. Acts, namely:- (a) - - - - -; (b) - - - - -; (c) - - - - -; (d) - - - - -; (e) - - - - -; (f) - - - - -; (g) - - - - -; (ii) any offence punishable under any other law providing for the prevention of hoarding or profiteering or of adulteration of food or drugs or of corruption, or (g) is so desperate and dangerous as to render his being at large without security hazardous to the community, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bail bond, for his KL,J good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three years, as the Magistrate thinks fit." As per Section - 173 (1) of the BNSS, every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge KL,J of a police station, and if given (i) orally, it shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid, shall be signed by the person giving it; (ii) by electronic communication, it shall be taken on record by him on being signed within three days by the person giving it, and the substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such Officer in such form as the State Government may by rules Veerla Sudhakar vs The State Of Telangana, on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31201218/ 3 prescribe in this behalf. 10. In Banala Subhashini v. The State of Telangana 1, this Court had an occasion to deal with the scope and ambit of Section - 145 of the Code the powers of the Executive Magistrate, and by relying upon various judgments of Apex Court, it had held that the Executive Magistrate cannot pass any order, once there is anything to say that prima facie, any person in possession and once there is a civil matter pending. As per the said Section, when an Executive Magistrate receives information within his local jurisdiction, a person who, habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of offences, involving a breach of the peace, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond, with sureties, for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three (03) years, as the Magistrate thinks fit.
